In the fourth stage a line is drawn thro.en: In the fourth stage a line is drawn through the intercept point at right angles to the Zn direction. This line is the LOP. It represents every point where the ship could have been at the moment of the sight; the ship is somewhere on this line.

In the second stage a single line is dra.en: In the second stage a single line is drawn from the AP. This line is Zn and represents the direction in which the celestial body is seen. Zn is not a course and not the direction the ship is heading; it only carries the information “the body lies in this direction”, measured from true north.

In the third stage the difference betwee.en: In the third stage the difference between Ho and Hc is treated purely as a distance, taking 1′ = 1 nautical mile. This distance is laid off along the Zn line: towards the body if Ho > Hc, away from the body if Ho < Hc. There is still no LOP at this stage; only how far and in which direction the position lies from the AP is established.
